utilityName: City of Taylor Cross Connection Control Backflow
testingFrequency: Upon installation, repair, or relocation; annual thereafter
dueBasis: Taylor says all backflow protection assemblies must be tested upon installation, repair, or relocation and that all backflow assemblies should be tested annually.
officialListLabel: Find BPAT registered to work in Taylor
penalties: Taylor says testers no longer submit paper reports directly to the City; accepted reporting and BPAT registration run through VEPO/Envirotrax.
sourceExcerpt: Taylor publishes annual and event-triggered assembly testing, online VEPO submission, BPAT registration in Envirotrax, and fire sprinkler tester constraints.
verdictSummary: Taylor is a useful Central Texas VEPO page because it explicitly connects annual testing, irrigation context, paperless reporting, registered BPAT lookup, and fire sprinkler rules.
whoIsAffected: Taylor properties with backflow protection assemblies, irrigation systems, and fire protection sprinkler assemblies.
residentialNotes: Taylor names garden hoses and irrigation systems as common residential backflow concerns.
Irrigation users should confirm installation testing and any annual local code overlay before scheduling.
commercialNotes: Commercial owners should treat annual testing and VEPO submission as a single workflow.
Fire sprinkler assemblies need the State Fire Marshal employment overlay.

annualTesting.summary: Taylor says all assemblies should be tested annually after installation, repair, or relocation trigger testing.
highlights: BPAT approval follows license, insurance, and test accuracy verification.
workflowSteps: Confirm the assembly and due basis with Taylor's official page.
Find a BPAT registered to work in Taylor.
Have the BPAT submit the report through VEPO/Envirotrax.

irrigation.summary: Taylor gives specific irrigation guidance: TCEQ requires a licensed BPA tester to check the BPA when installed on an irrigation system, and local rules may require annual testing.
highlights: Installation testing is a direct TCEQ-linked trigger.
Taylor warns that water providers may add annual testing rules.
workflowSteps: Confirm whether the irrigation BPA is newly installed or locally due.
Use a licensed BPA tester registered for Taylor.
Submit through the VEPO route when the assembly is reportable.

fireLine.summary: Taylor states fire protection sprinkler assemblies must be tested or repaired by a BPAT who is a full-time employee of a licensed fire protection sprinkler company.
highlights: Fire sprinkler assemblies are named separately.
The State Fire Marshal overlay controls tester eligibility.
The Taylor VEPO route still controls registered BPAT status.
workflowSteps: Identify whether the assembly serves fire protection sprinklers.
Use a BPAT employed by a licensed fire protection sprinkler company.
Have the report submitted through the accepted Taylor VEPO path.
Use Taylor's cross-connection page to classify annual, irrigation, or fire-line context.
Find a BPAT registered to work in Taylor.
Do not treat a paper report as the accepted City workflow.
failureHighlights: Paper reports are not the current Taylor reporting path.
A BPAT must clear license, insurance, and test accuracy verification before approved-list addition.
Irrigation and fire-line rules have separate eligibility details.

costBand.testingRange: Private Taylor test prices vary by assembly type and whether irrigation or fire-line work is involved.
costBand.repairRetestRange: Repair and retest pricing depends on device condition and fire-line requirements.
costBand.pricingNotes: The practical cost risk is using a tester who cannot complete the Taylor VEPO submission.
